title: Paint-Anything: Unified Any-Color Control for Image Generation and Editing
why_read: A practical image-generation control method letting users specify exact hex color values for objects, useful for design workflows but a narrow, incremental capability.
analysis: Paint-Anything lets a diffusion image model take a precise 24-bit hex color code and apply it faithfully to a specific object during generation or editing, which prior methods handled only loosely or with specialized machinery. The authors built a large training dataset (Paint-500K) by grounding objects in real photos and labeling their colors, then supplemented it with synthetic 'pure-color anchor' examples to handle cases like shadows that make real photos only approximate the target color. Tested on the FLUX.2-4B model, it substantially improves color-fidelity benchmarks over the base model. This is a useful, if narrow, engineering contribution for professional design tools rather than a fundamental advance in image generation.
